newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares dive at noon as bank funds curbed.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares dive at noon as bank funds curbed.

text.p: Shenzhen shares suffered broad losses on Friday morning after Beijing announced measures to block state bank funds from flowing into the heated stock markets, brokers said.
The foreign currency B share index plunged 6.05 points or 3.86 percent to 150.72 on turnover of HK$42.7 million.
The domestic currency A share index fell 27.95 points or 5.92 percent to 444.54 after opening at a low of 433.76 points. Turnover was 7.2 billion yuan.
Beijing on Thursday ordered state banks to begin unwinding positions on the stock exchanges on Friday and to cease trading treasury debt repurchase (repo) agreements.
"By drying up the bank funds, liqudity on both the stock markets and the debt markets will fall significantly," an analyst at PBI Securities said.
Under the new measures, issued by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, all state banks must offset their share positions within 10 days.
Analysts said as much as half of stock market liquidity had come from banks via the repo market.
The bank fund curb follows a series of government measures to reduce the amount of so-called hot money, or speculative funds, entering the overheated market.
The government recently banned all state firms and listed companies from speculative stock trading.
Both indices are likely to stay in deep negative territory in the afternoon session as there is no immediate news to help them back up, brokers said.
But analysts said they expected sentiment to pick up later in June during the run-up to the reversion of the British colony of Hong Kong to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
No B shares gained in morning trading, with Weifu Fuel Injection Co the sharpest loser, falling to its 10 percent limit-down level of HK$4.95.
A number of A shares approached their daily 10 percent limit-down levels.
Appliance maker Gansu Changfeng fell 9.44 percent to 5.47 yuan.
